POWER BI CASE STUDY

FreshBites Restaurant Group profitability analysis

Sales increased in 2026, but margin pressure and operating losses meant the business retained less value from that growth. This report traces the change across food cost, discounts, labor, waste, and branches.

THE PROBLEM

Growth did not produce the expected profitability

FreshBites Restaurant Group grew sales in 2026, but kept less gross profit from each dollar sold. The goal was to identify how food costs, discounting, labor, and waste affected performance across branches.

THE CONCLUSION

Higher costs outweighed the gross-profit gain

Net sales rose 14.1% to $3.99M, while gross margin fell 2.78 percentage points to 63.53%. Food cost grew 23.6%, discount spend 54.8%, and waste and spoilage 58.5%. Gross profit dollars increased, but higher labor and inventory losses outweighed that gain.

A tracked contribution measure—gross profit less labor, waste, and spoilage—declined by about $447K. This measure excludes other operating expenses and is therefore not net profit.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH

A model designed for consistent branch and period comparisons

  • Prepared and related sales, inventory, labor, target, branch, promotion, employee, menu, and date data.
  • Used a dimensional model to keep business measures consistent across report pages.
  • Compared 2025 and 2026 results across revenue, margins, discounts, labor, and waste.
  • Separated the tracked contribution measure from net profit to avoid overstating the conclusion.

Tools

Power BI, Power Query, DAX

Techniques

Data modeling, KPI design, variance analysis, branch benchmarking
